projects.title: CLI Expense Tracker
projects.summary: A command-line tool that records expenses to a CSV file and prints monthly summaries.
projects.brief:
Build `expenses.py`, a command-line app with three subcommands:

- `add <amount> <category> [--note TEXT] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]` appends a row to `expenses.csv`.
- `list [--month YYYY-MM]` prints matching expenses as an aligned table.
- `summary --month YYYY-MM` prints the total per category, sorted by amount, plus the grand total.

Use only the standard library (`argparse`, `csv`, `datetime`, `decimal`). Money must never be stored as a float.

milestones.title: Model and storage
milestones.description: Write load/save functions for expenses using csv.DictReader/DictWriter; create the file with a header if it does not exist.

milestones.title: add command
milestones.description: Parse and validate amount (Decimal, > 0), category and optional date; append one row.

milestones.title: list and summary
milestones.description: Filter by month, group with a dict or collections.Counter, print aligned output.

milestones.title: Errors
milestones.description: Friendly messages and non-zero exit codes for bad input, missing or corrupt files; no tracebacks for user mistakes.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: pytest tests for parsing, grouping and a round trip through a temporary CSV file (tmp_path).

rubric.lookFor: Parsing, storage and reporting are separate functions; main() only wires them.
Totals are exact (Decimal) and month filtering handles edge dates.
Clear names, type hints, no duplicated formatting code.
Bad amounts, unknown dates and a corrupt row are reported clearly and the program does not crash.
Tests cover happy paths and at least two failure cases without touching the real data file.
You can explain why Decimal and not float, and how the CSV schema could evolve.

stretchGoals: Budgets per category with a warning when exceeded
Package it with a console_scripts entry point

projects.title: Async Link Checker
projects.summary: Crawl one website concurrently and report broken links, with a polite concurrency limit.
projects.brief:
Write `linkcheck`, which takes a start URL and crawls pages on the same host up to `--max-pages` (default 200). For every link found, report broken ones (4xx, 5xx, timeouts) with the page they were found on.

Use `asyncio` with an HTTP client such as `aiohttp` or `httpx`. Limit concurrency with an `asyncio.Semaphore` (`--concurrency`, default 10), set timeouts, and never fetch the same URL twice.

milestones.title: Fetch one page
milestones.description: Async function that fetches a URL with a timeout and extracts absolute links (urllib.parse.urljoin).

milestones.title: Crawl with a queue
milestones.description: asyncio.Queue plus worker tasks; a visited set; stay on the start host; stop at max pages.

milestones.title: Politeness
milestones.description: Semaphore-based concurrency limit, a per-request timeout, and a User-Agent header.

milestones.title: Report
milestones.description: Group broken links by status, print a summary, exit code 1 if anything is broken.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: Test link extraction and crawl logic against a fake fetcher, without real network calls.

rubric.lookFor: Fetching, parsing and crawling are separate; the fetcher can be swapped for a fake.
No duplicate fetches; host boundary and max-pages respected.
No blocking calls inside coroutines; tasks are awaited or cancelled cleanly.
Timeouts, DNS failures and non-HTML responses are handled per URL without killing the crawl.
Async tests with a fake fetcher cover cycles and broken links.
You can explain why a semaphore and not just more workers, and where the event loop could block.

projects.title: Kanban Board
projects.summary: A Trello-style board with columns, cards, editing and persistence in localStorage.
projects.brief:
Build a single-page Kanban board with three default columns (To do, Doing, Done). Users can add, edit, delete and move cards between columns (buttons are fine; drag and drop is a stretch goal). State persists in localStorage and survives a reload.

Keep state in one place with `useReducer`, and make every action a pure reducer case.

milestones.title: Static layout
milestones.description: Column and Card components rendered from hard-coded data via props.

milestones.title: Reducer
milestones.description: useReducer with add, edit, delete and move actions; the reducer is pure and exported.

milestones.title: Forms
milestones.description: Controlled inputs to add and edit cards, with validation (no empty titles).

milestones.title: Persistence
milestones.description: A custom hook useLocalStorageState that loads once and saves on change.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: Unit tests for the reducer and one React Testing Library test that adds and moves a card.

rubric.lookFor: Clear component tree; state lives in one reducer, components stay presentational.
Moves, edits and deletes never lose or duplicate cards; reload restores state.
Keys are stable ids (not indexes); no unnecessary effects.
Corrupt localStorage data falls back to defaults without crashing.
Reducer tests cover every action; one UI test covers a real user flow.
You can explain why useReducer here and what would change with a backend.

projects.title: Weather Dashboard
projects.summary: Search cities and show current weather and a 5-day forecast from a public API.
projects.brief:
Build a dashboard that searches a city, shows current conditions and a 5-day forecast, and remembers the last five searches. Use a public API such as Open-Meteo (no key needed).

Every request must show a loading state, a friendly error, and an empty state; cancel stale requests when the user types a new search.

milestones.title: API layer
milestones.description: A small module with fetch functions and typed responses, separate from components.

milestones.title: useWeather hook
milestones.description: Custom hook exposing data, loading and error; aborts stale requests with AbortController.

milestones.title: UI states
milestones.description: Skeletons while loading, retry on error, an empty state before the first search.

milestones.title: Recent searches
milestones.description: Persist the last five cities and let the user re-run them.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: Mock fetch and test the hook's loading, success and error transitions.

rubric.lookFor: API calls live outside components; components render state only.
Units and dates are correct; stale responses never overwrite newer ones.
No fetching in render; effects have correct dependencies.
Network errors, empty results and rate limits each get a clear message.
Hook tests cover success, failure and cancellation.
You can explain the race condition you prevented and how.

projects.title: Library Management Core
projects.summary: Domain model and service for books, members and loans, driven from a small console menu.
projects.brief:
Model `Book`, `Member` and `Loan` (prefer records where it fits). A `LibraryService` lets members borrow and return books, enforces a limit of 3 active loans, computes overdue fines, and reports the most borrowed books using streams.

Rules violations throw specific checked or unchecked exceptions you design.

milestones.title: Domain model
milestones.description: Immutable records and enums; equals/hashCode correct; ids as value types.

milestones.title: Service rules
milestones.description: Borrow, return, loan limit, availability; in-memory repositories behind interfaces.

milestones.title: Reports with streams
milestones.description: Overdue loans, fines, top 5 books, members with no loans.

milestones.title: Exceptions
milestones.description: Custom exceptions with clear messages; the menu catches them and keeps running.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: JUnit 5 tests for every rule, using a fixed Clock for dates.

rubric.lookFor: Domain, service and repository layers are distinct; the console menu is thin.
Loan limit, availability and fines are always correct.
Records, Optional and streams used idiomatically; no raw types.
Rule violations are modelled as exceptions, never silent failures.
Tests use a fixed Clock and cover each rule's edge cases.
You can explain your exception design and why repositories are interfaces.

stretchGoals: Spring Boot REST layer on top

projects.title: URL Shortener API
projects.summary: A REST API that creates short links, redirects, and counts clicks.
projects.brief:
Build an HTTP API (Express or Fastify):

- `POST /links` with `{ url }` returns `{ code, shortUrl }`; invalid URLs get 400.
- `GET /:code` redirects with 302 and increments a click counter; unknown codes get 404.
- `GET /links/:code/stats` returns clicks and createdAt.

Store data in SQLite or a JSON file behind a repository module. Add request logging and graceful shutdown.

milestones.title: Skeleton
milestones.description: App factory function (for tests), routes, JSON body parsing, a health endpoint.

milestones.title: Codes and storage
milestones.description: Collision-safe short codes; a repository module with create, find and increment.

milestones.title: Validation and errors
milestones.description: Schema validation; one central error handler with consistent error JSON.

milestones.title: Production basics
milestones.description: Structured logging, config from environment variables, SIGTERM graceful shutdown.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: Supertest (or inject) tests for create, redirect, 404 and validation.

rubric.lookFor: Routes, validation and storage are separate modules; the app is built by a factory.
Redirects, counters and collisions are correct under repeated calls.
Async errors never become unhandled rejections; no callback pyramids.
Bad input, unknown codes and storage failures return the right status codes.
API tests run against an in-memory or temp store.
You can explain how you would scale reads and prevent abuse.

projects.title: Concurrent File Downloader
projects.summary: Download a list of URLs in parallel with a worker pool, progress output and cancellation.
projects.brief:
Write a CLI that reads URLs from a file and downloads them into a directory using a worker pool (`-workers`, default 4). Show progress, support Ctrl+C cancellation through `context.Context`, and print a final report of successes and failures.

Wrap errors with `%w` and make the downloader testable with `httptest.Server`.

milestones.title: Single download
milestones.description: Function that downloads one URL to a file with a context and timeout.

milestones.title: Worker pool
milestones.description: Jobs and results channels, N workers, WaitGroup; no goroutine leaks.

milestones.title: Cancellation
milestones.description: signal.NotifyContext; partial files are cleaned up on cancel.

milestones.title: Report
milestones.description: Collect results, print a summary, exit non-zero when anything failed.

milestones.title: Tests
milestones.description: httptest.Server tests for success, 404 and cancellation; run with -race.

rubric.lookFor: Download logic is independent of the CLI and of the pool.
Every URL is processed exactly once; results match inputs.
Channels closed by the sender; no data races (go test -race passes).
Errors are wrapped with context and reported per URL.
Tests use httptest and cover cancellation.
You can explain who closes which channel and why.

projects.title: Design a URL Shortener at Scale
projects.summary: A written system design: 100M new links a month, 10:1 read to write, low-latency redirects.
projects.brief:
Write a design document (2-4 pages, diagrams welcome) for a URL shortener handling 100 million new links per month with a 10:1 read to write ratio and p99 redirect latency under 50 ms.

Cover requirements, capacity estimates, API, data model, key generation, storage choice, caching, scaling and failure modes. Be explicit about trade-offs.

milestones.title: Requirements and estimates
milestones.description: Functional and non-functional requirements; QPS, storage over 5 years, bandwidth.

milestones.title: API and data model
milestones.description: Endpoints, schema, and how codes are generated without collisions.

milestones.title: High-level design
milestones.description: Diagram with load balancer, services, database, cache; the redirect path end to end.

milestones.title: Scaling and reliability
milestones.description: Sharding or partitioning, cache strategy and invalidation, replication, failure modes.

milestones.title: Trade-offs
milestones.description: At least three explicit decisions with the alternatives you rejected and why.

rubric.lookFor: Scope is clear and estimates are realistic and shown.
Schema and key generation are justified.
Read path is cached and storage is partitioned sensibly.
Single points of failure and failure behaviour are addressed.
Alternatives are compared honestly.
The document is structured and easy to follow.

projects.title: E-commerce Schema and Queries
projects.summary: Design a PostgreSQL schema for a small shop and write the reporting queries it needs.
projects.brief:
Design tables for customers, products, inventory, orders and order items in PostgreSQL. Write migrations, seed realistic data (at least 10k orders, generated with SQL), and answer these with queries: monthly revenue, top products per category (window functions), customers with no orders in 90 days, and inventory that would go negative.

Add the indexes your queries need and prove it with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

milestones.title: Schema
milestones.description: Tables with primary and foreign keys, NOT NULL, CHECK constraints, money as numeric.

milestones.title: Migrations and seed
milestones.description: Versioned migration files and a generate_series based seed script.

milestones.title: Reporting queries
milestones.description: The four required queries, using CTEs and window functions where they help.

milestones.title: Indexes
milestones.description: Indexes justified by EXPLAIN ANALYZE before and after.

milestones.title: Transactions
milestones.description: Place an order in one transaction that also decrements inventory safely.

rubric.lookFor: Normalised where it matters, with sensible constraints.
Queries return correct results on edge cases.
Indexes are justified with real plans.
Order placement cannot oversell under concurrency.
Schema changes are versioned and repeatable.
You can explain each index and isolation choice.

projects.title: Containerise a Web App Stack
projects.summary: Package an API, a database and a reverse proxy with Docker Compose, production style.
projects.brief:
Take any small web API (for example the URL shortener project) and containerise it: a multi-stage Dockerfile producing a small non-root image, plus a `compose.yaml` with the API, PostgreSQL and an nginx reverse proxy.

Add healthchecks, named volumes, environment-based config with secrets kept out of the image, and a Makefile or script to run it.

milestones.title: Dockerfile
milestones.description: Multi-stage build, pinned base image, non-root user, .dockerignore; image size noted.

milestones.title: Compose stack
milestones.description: API, database and proxy services with depends_on on healthy services.

milestones.title: Config and secrets
milestones.description: Environment variables and Compose secrets; nothing sensitive baked into layers.

milestones.title: Healthchecks and volumes
milestones.description: Healthchecks for each service, a named volume for data, restart policies.

milestones.title: Verification
milestones.description: A script that builds, starts, waits for health, hits an endpoint and tears down.

rubric.lookFor: Small, reproducible, non-root, cache-friendly layer order.
Services start in the right order and recover from restarts.
No secrets in the image; minimal attack surface.
Healthchecks and logs make problems visible.
One command builds and verifies the stack.
You can explain each layer and Compose choice.

stretchGoals: CI job that builds and scans the image
